title: Mixed L/NL Operational Regime
purpose: Define a mixed L/NL operational regime in which L-classified and NL-classified continuation components coexist under explicit separation without introducing a third primitive foundation.

motivation.problem: The framework already governs L, NL, and their boundary, but mixed continuation cases still lack a dedicated derived regime classification.
motivation.resolution: Mixed L/NL behavior is classified as a derived RT operational regime with explicit component separation and RT_core traceability.

core_definition.mixed_lnl_regime: An RT operational regime in which L-classified and NL-classified continuation components coexist under explicitly separated domain, scale, context, or orientation partitions.
core_definition.trace_requirement: Every mixed-regime classification must constructively trace to RT_core.

governance_rules.name: No Third Foundation
governance_rules.statement: Mixed L/NL regimes do not constitute a third primitive regime.

governance_rules.name: Explicit Component Declaration
governance_rules.statement: Every mixed regime must declare which components are L-classified and which are NL-classified.

governance_rules.name: Explicit Separation Basis
governance_rules.statement: The separation basis must be explicit: domain, scale, context, orientation partition, or admissibility layer.

governance_rules.name: Default To NL When Unseparated
governance_rules.statement: If the L/NL components cannot be separated, the regime defaults to NL-classification until proven otherwise.

governance_rules.name: RT Trace Bound
governance_rules.statement: Mixed-regime classification remains trace-bound to RT_core.

examples.local_linear_global_nonlinear: A regime may be locally L-classified while globally NL-classified due to residue or feedback deformation.
examples.scale_split: A regime may be L-classified at one scale and NL-classified at another.
examples.context_split: A regime may preserve L-composition under one admissibility context while becoming NL under another.

effects: Registers mixed L/NL behavior as a derived RT operational regime.
Requires explicit separation of L-classified and NL-classified components.
Preserves RT_core as the trace source and keeps NL as the fallback when separation fails.

notes: Existing RT, L, NL, and boundary definitions remain canonical.
Mixed L/NL regimes do not alter RT_core or introduce a third primitive regime.
Future representation rules can attach to this mixed regime without revising the core calculus.
Mixed L/NL regimes remain derived classifications and do not supersede RT_core.
Unseparated mixed cases default to NL-classification until the separation basis is declared.
This patch is governance and architecture only.
Mixed L/NL continuation is derived under explicit separation and remains trace-bound to the canonical root expression.
